title: ASML Holding N.V. (ASML) vs. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSM): A Key Supplier Says it Can Keep Up With the AI Boom

content_html:
Zeiss, the German optics maker whose mirrors are critical to ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ:ASML)'s most advanced chipmaking machines, said this week that it's confident it has the capacity to handle booming AI-driven demand. The statement pushes back on investor worries about bottlenecks in the AI supply chain, worries that touch nearly every company racing to build AI infrastructure right now.

Why One Supplier's Confidence Matters So Much

ASML is the only company in the world that makes machines capable of producing the most cutting-edge AI chips. Zeiss's ultra-precise mirrors, which take months to build, are one of the most delicate links in that chain. Zeiss says its components already play a role in producing about 80% of the world's chips, and it's building out its headquarters and a new factory to keep pace. Zeiss's semiconductor division head, Frank Rohmund, called this "the real, long-term items when it comes to capacity expansion." The timing matters: this comes right as ASML raised its own 2026 sales outlook, and as its biggest customer, TSMC, reported record profits driven by that same AI demand.

This makes you wonder: if the industry's most critical, hardest-to-replace supplier says it can keep up, does that put AI bottleneck fears to rest, or is Zeiss's confidence just one link in a chain with plenty of other places to break?

ASML's Bull and Bear Case

ASML Holding N.V. (NASDAQ:ASML) raised its 2026 annual sales outlook to between $49.3 billion and $51.6 billion, citing "extremely strong" AI-driven tool orders. It holds a complete monopoly in EUV lithography, with no real rival at the high end of the market, and shipped 48 systems last year, with 65 forecast this year and 85 in 2027. That's made it Europe's most valuable company, as per Reuters. Its critical mirror supplier now says it's confident it can handle demand too, addressing one of the biggest fears investors have had about the AI supply chain. Rohmund even said ASML and Zeiss have a roadmap that extends to "2040 or so."

However, ASML depends entirely on a small number of irreplaceable suppliers for parts that take months to build, Zeiss for mirrors, Germany's Trumpf for lasers, which means a single bottleneck anywhere in that chain could delay ASML's own delivery schedule. Rohmund's own confidence came with a warning attached: "Sooner or later, most likely, there will be some kind of correction," he said.

ASML also carries real geopolitical risk. U.S. export restrictions already block its most advanced tools from China, and lawmakers have proposed expanding those curbs to cover more of its older machines too, which would also hit Zeiss's own business supplying lenses for them.

content_html_zh:
德国光学制造商蔡司（Zeiss）的镜子对 ASML Holding N.V. 至关重要。 （纳斯达克股票代码：ASML）最先进的芯片制造机器本周表示，它有信心有能力应对蓬勃发展的人工智能驱动的需求。 该声明打消了投资者对人工智能供应链瓶颈的担忧，这种担忧几乎触及目前所有竞相建设人工智能基础设施的公司。

为什么供应商的信心如此重要

ASML是世界上唯一一家制造能够生产最尖端人工智能芯片的机器的公司。 蔡司的超精密镜子需要数月的时间才能制造出来，是该链条中最微妙的环节之一。 蔡司表示，其零部件已在全球约 80% 的芯片生产中发挥着重要作用，并且正在建设总部和新工厂以跟上步伐。 蔡司半导体部门负责人 Frank Rohmund 称这是“产能扩张方面真正的长期项目”。 时机很重要：恰逢 ASML 上调了 2026 年的销售前景，而其最大客户台积电 (TSMC) 在同样的人工智能需求推动下公布了创纪录的利润。

这让你想知道：如果这个行业最关键、最难取代的供应商表示自己可以跟上，这是否可以消除对人工智能瓶颈的担忧，或者蔡司的信心只是链条中的一个环节，还有很多其他地方需要打破？

ASML 的牛市和熊市案例

阿斯麦控股有限公司 ASML（纳斯达克股票代码：ASML）将 2026 年销售额预期上调至 493 亿美元至 516 亿美元之间，理由是人工智能驱动工具订单“极其强劲”。 它在 EUV 光刻领域拥有完全垄断地位，在高端市场没有真正的竞争对手，去年出货了 48 套系统，今年预测为 65 套，2027 年为 85 套。 据路透社报道，这使其成为欧洲最有价值的公司。 其关键的镜子供应商现在表示，它有信心也能满足需求，解决投资者对人工智能供应链最大的担忧之一。 Rohmund甚至表示ASML和蔡司有一个延伸到“2040年左右”的路线图。

然而，ASML 完全依赖于少数不可替代的供应商来生产需要数月时间制造的零部件，例如镜子的蔡司、激光器的德国通快，这意味着该供应链中任何地方的单一瓶颈都可能会延迟 ASML 自己的交付时间表。 罗蒙德自己的信心伴随着警告：“迟早，很可能会出现某种纠正，”他说。

ASML 还面临着真正的地缘政治风险。 美国的出口限制已经阻止了其最先进的工具从中国进口，立法者提议扩大这些限制，以涵盖更多的旧机器，这也会打击蔡司自己的镜头供应业务。
